name: Map request values to owned classes before instantiating
query: This plugin runs new $format() with a class name taken from $_POST['format'] after sanitize_key(). Fix it so the request cannot create classes the plugin does not own, and only authorized users can run an export.
expected_behavior: Step 1: Explain that sanitize_key() keeps the name well-formed but does not stop the request from choosing which class is created
Step 2: Replace the dynamic class name with a hardcoded map from request values to classes the plugin owns
Step 3: Verify the nonce before the protected work
Step 4: Reject a request value that is not a key in the map with a 400 response before any capability check or instantiation
Step 5: Check the capability, such as manage_options, and return 403 before instantiating the mapped class
Step 6: Instantiate only the mapped class and keep every class and method in the example defined
success_criteria: A request value outside the map is rejected without creating any class
An invalid nonce and a denied capability both stop before instantiation
Only the owned, mapped classes can be created
The nonce and capability checks do not replace the allowlist, and the allowlist does not replace them
The example calls no undefined function or class
